summary: Still focused heavily on ash processing today. Discovered a broken underground belt near the coal mine, which meant coal production had been running at roughly half capacity. That explains several of the recent supply inconsistencies.
There were also additional issues with coal delivery, but after some restructuring I managed to optimize the coal mine layout. Output is now stable and more consistent.

I relocated the burner turbines and fuel processors closer to the coal mine. Centralizing everything has simplified logistics significantly — shorter belt runs, fewer choke points, and clearer flow paths.
Power is finally stable. We are running 7 burner turbines for a total of 14 MW capacity. However, that stability comes at a cost: the turbines now generate two full belts of ash.
With 4 solid separators active, we are roughly keeping pace — about 40 ash processed per second versus 38–42 ash produced per second. It’s tight, but sustainable for now.
We also surpassed 1 million total ash produced today. Not exactly the milestone I was hoping to celebrate.

On the research front, I completed Moss - Stage 1. Like Botany, it doesn’t immediately solve a pressing issue, but it leads directly into Wood Processing — which is critical. My wood stockpile has been depleted again. I want Wood Processing researched tomorrow if possible.

Tonight was brutal. Three breaches occurred simultaneously. I could only respond to one at a time. While production remained intact, the defensive walls took serious damage. Repairs will be necessary before the next wave.

status.resource: Coal production optimized; wood stockpile depleted again.
status.science: Moss - Stage 1 researched; aiming for Wood Processing next.
status.defense: Three simultaneous breaches; walls heavily damaged.

todo: Repair and reinforce damaged wall sections.
Monitor ash balance to prevent overflow.
